activities.name: Select Production Model
activities.description: Identify and document production AI model with baseline performance characteristics

narratives.name: How to Perform
narratives.description: Model selection technique and best practices

narrativeContexts.context: Model selection establishes the foundation for optimization efforts by identifying appropriate model architecture and validating baseline performance.

Begin by gathering use case requirements including task type for text generation, completion, or chat, performance constraints for latency and throughput, and accuracy expectations. Evaluate candidate models from validated model catalog considering model architecture such as decoder-only or mixture-of-experts, parameter count from 7B to 70B+, and baseline performance metrics. Document source model location in HuggingFace repository or model registry, version, and license. Establish baseline accuracy metrics by running representative test datasets. Specify target hardware platform including GPU type, memory, and count based on model size and performance requirements. Document use case and expected workload characteristics including prompt lengths and generation patterns.

Avoid selecting models without validating hardware compatibility and memory requirements. Do not skip baseline performance measurement which provides quantitative optimization targets. Validate model license compatibility with production use case.

activities.name: Define Optimization Strategy
activities.description: Select quantization approach and establish validation methodology based on requirements

narratives.name: How to Perform

narrativeContexts.context: Defining optimization strategy ensures systematic approach to model compression aligned with performance and quality requirements.

Analyze model architecture and baseline performance to determine appropriate quantization format. Choose INT4 for maximum compression with 4x reduction and moderate accuracy impact of 3-5% degradation, INT8 for balanced performance with 2x reduction and 1-3% degradation, FP8 for hardware-optimized scenarios on supported accelerators, or NVFP4 for extreme compression needs. Establish accuracy tolerance thresholds based on business requirements and use case sensitivity. Set target latency and throughput goals for production workload considering SLA requirements. Identify memory constraints based on available GPU memory per accelerator. Define validation methodology specifying test datasets with representative samples covering use case diversity, accuracy metrics such as perplexity and task-specific scores, and acceptance criteria. Configure optimization toolkit LLM Compressor with selected parameters and calibration dataset.

Avoid selecting quantization format without considering hardware support and accuracy-performance tradeoffs. Do not establish unrealistic accuracy thresholds that prevent any compression. Validate toolkit version compatibility with target model architecture.

activities.name: Quantize Language Model
activities.description: Execute quantization process to compress model using optimization toolkit

narratives.name: How to Perform

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations initiate model quantization by selecting an appropriate quantization format based on requirements for size reduction, inference performance, and acceptable accuracy degradation.

Begin by loading the source model from HuggingFace or model repositories, configure the LLM Compressor with target quantization format INT4, INT8, FP8, or NVFP4, calibration dataset, and accuracy tolerance thresholds. Execute quantization transformations systematically while monitoring accuracy impact. The toolkit applies quantization to model weights, achieving 50-75% size reduction depending on format. Generate quantized model artifacts in safetensors format compatible with vLLM runtime. Document quantization parameters, toolkit version, and execution metadata.

Avoid selecting quantization format without considering hardware support and accuracy impact. Do not skip calibration datasets which optimize quantization parameters. Validate compatibility with vLLM runtime early to prevent deployment failures.

activities.name: Validate Quantized Model
activities.description: Execute test suite comparing quantized model outputs against baseline for accuracy verification

narratives.name: How to Perform

narrativeContexts.context: Validating quantized model accuracy ensures compression techniques preserve model quality within acceptable tolerances before production deployment.

Establish comprehensive test dataset representing diversity of production inputs including typical use cases, edge cases, and challenging scenarios. Document appropriate accuracy metrics such as perplexity for language models, BLEU scores for translation, and task-specific accuracy. Execute baseline measurements running original unquantized model against test dataset, recording detailed accuracy metrics and output quality. Run quantized model against identical test dataset using same metrics. Compare quantized model metrics against baseline with statistical analysis, allowing small accuracy degradation of 1-3% for INT8 and 3-5% for INT4 based on compression ratios. Identify specific scenarios where quantization causes noticeable degradation. Generate comprehensive validation report with recommendation for production deployment or further optimization.

Avoid using non-representative test datasets that miss edge cases. Do not accept accuracy degradation exceeding business-defined thresholds. Validate statistical significance of differences rather than relying on single metric comparisons.

activities.name: Benchmark Inference Performance
activities.description: Measure latency, throughput, and resource utilization under representative workload conditions

narratives.name: How to Perform

narrativeContexts.context: Comprehensive inference performance benchmarking provides quantitative data on service capabilities, identifies optimization opportunities, and validates that deployments meet SLA requirements.

Define representative workload scenarios accurately reflecting production usage patterns including typical request sizes, prompt lengths, generation token counts, and request arrival patterns. Warm up inference service to ensure model caching and optimizations reach steady state before measurements. Execute benchmarks submitting requests at controlled rates while measuring latency at percentiles P50, P90, P95, and P99, throughput as requests per second and tokens per second, and resource utilization including GPU utilization, GPU memory consumption, and batch processing efficiency. Gradually increase concurrent request load to identify saturation point and optimal batch sizes. For distributed deployments, measure how performance scales with additional GPUs. Generate comprehensive performance reports documenting measured capabilities, comparing results against SLA requirements, identifying bottlenecks, and providing optimization recommendations. Calculate cost per request and cost per generated token for cost optimization.

Avoid cold start measurements that include model loading time. Do not use non-representative workload patterns that miss production diversity. Validate steady-state performance rather than transient spikes.

activities.name: Configure vLLM Integration
activities.description: Configure vLLM runtime parameters for optimized model loading and inference

narratives.name: How to Perform

narrativeContexts.context: Configuring vLLM integration ensures quantized models load correctly with optimal runtime parameters for inference performance.

Configure model loading settings specifying model path in HuggingFace repository, local filesystem, or OCI registry, model format including HuggingFace, vLLM native, or OCI modelcar, and tokenizer configuration. Set runtime parameters governing inference performance including tensor-parallel-size for distributing model weights across multiple GPUs, gpu-memory-utilization controlling GPU memory allocation typically 0.8-0.9, and maximum sequence length max-model-len and batch size max-num-batched-tokens impacting throughput and latency. Configure KV cache quantization kv-cache-dtype to reduce memory consumption. Validate configuration by starting vLLM service and confirming model loads successfully without errors, responds correctly to test inference requests, and achieves expected performance characteristics.

Avoid tensor parallelism configurations exceeding available GPU count. Do not set memory utilization too high over 0.95 causing out-of-memory failures. Validate quantization format compatibility with vLLM runtime version.

activities.name: Configure vLLM Inference Server
activities.description: Set runtime parameters, model loading configuration, and API settings for inference service

narratives.name: Configuration Technique
narratives.description: vLLM server configuration approach and best practices

narrativeContexts.context: vLLM server configuration requires comprehensive understanding of model loading, tensor parallelism, memory management, and API compatibility parameters to optimize inference performance and enable application integration.

Start by specifying model path and format (HuggingFace, OCI container, or filesystem). Configure tensor-parallel-size to match GPU count for distributed model weights. Set gpu-memory-utilization to 0.8-0.9 for optimal memory usage. Define max-model-len and max-num-batched-tokens based on workload characteristics. Enable OpenAI-compatible API endpoints with appropriate CORS and authentication settings. Configure advanced features like KV cache quantization, prefix caching, and speculative decoding based on performance requirements. Validate configuration by starting service locally and verifying model loads without errors.

Avoid setting tensor-parallel-size incorrectly (must match available GPU count). Do not exceed gpu-memory-utilization beyond 0.95 as this causes OOM errors. Ensure max-model-len does not exceed model's maximum sequence length. Verify tokenizer compatibility with model architecture. Test configuration changes in non-production before deploying to production.

activities.name: Design Distributed Inference Architecture
activities.description: Design multi-GPU distributed inference topology with parallelism strategy and communication patterns

narratives.name: Architecture Design Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Distributed inference architecture design balances model size constraints, GPU availability, network topology, and performance requirements to create scalable serving infrastructure.

Calculate model memory footprint and determine minimum GPU count for sharding. Select tensor parallelism degree based on GPU count per node (typically 2, 4, or 8 GPUs). Decide whether single-node multi-GPU or multi-node distribution is required based on model size. For multi-node scenarios, design leader-worker topology using LeaderWorkerSet pattern. Specify network communication requirements (NVLink for single-node, high-bandwidth Ethernet or InfiniBand for multi-node). Document architecture with topology diagrams showing model sharding and GPU allocation.

Avoid underestimating network bandwidth requirements for multi-node distribution. Do not design multi-node topology if model fits on single-node multi-GPU as this adds unnecessary complexity. Ensure GPU memory capacity accounts for both model weights and KV cache. Validate that cluster has sufficient GPU resources before finalizing architecture.

activities.name: Prepare Kubernetes Platform for AI
activities.description: Validate cluster prerequisites and prepare Kubernetes infrastructure for AI workloads

narratives.name: Platform Preparation Technique
narratives.description: Kubernetes cluster preparation for AI inference

narrativeContexts.context: Platform preparation validates that Kubernetes cluster meets version, networking, and access requirements before installing GPU operators and AI workloads.

Verify Kubernetes version is 1.33 or later using kubectl version. Confirm cluster-admin or sufficient RBAC permissions. Test network connectivity and DNS resolution. Configure kubectl context for target cluster. Verify container registry access to registry.redhat.io using pull secret. Validate Red Hat subscription entitlements include AI products. Document cluster configuration and access procedures.

Avoid skipping version validation as older Kubernetes versions lack required CRD features. Do not proceed without cluster-admin permissions as GPU operator installation requires cluster-level resources. Ensure registry pull secrets are configured in target namespace before deploying workloads. Verify DNS works correctly as service discovery depends on it.

activities.name: Install GPU Operators on Kubernetes
activities.description: Deploy Node Feature Discovery and NVIDIA GPU operators to enable GPU scheduling

narratives.name: GPU Operator Installation Technique

narrativeContexts.context: GPU operators enable Kubernetes to discover, schedule, and monitor GPU resources by deploying Node Feature Discovery for hardware detection and NVIDIA GPU Operator for GPU device plugins and drivers.

Create OperatorGroup and Subscription for Node Feature Discovery (NFD) Operator from Red Hat catalog. Verify NFD pods running and GPU feature labels appearing on nodes. Install NVIDIA GPU Operator via OperatorHub or Helm chart. Configure GPU Operator to match cluster environment (OpenShift vs upstream Kubernetes). Verify GPU device plugin pods running on all GPU nodes. Check that nvidia.com/gpu resources appear in node capacity. For multi-GPU nodes with NVSwitch, validate NVIDIA Fabric Manager deployed. Test GPU scheduling by deploying test workload requesting GPU resources.

Avoid installing GPU Operator before NFD as GPU feature detection depends on NFD. Do not modify GPU Operator default settings unless required by environment. Ensure GPU nodes have correct labels and taints before deploying workloads. Verify driver compatibility between GPU Operator version and GPU hardware generation. Monitor operator logs for errors during deployment.

activities.name: Deploy Standalone Inference Service
activities.description: Install Red Hat AI Inference using Helm chart with configured values for standalone deployment

narratives.name: Standalone Deployment Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Helm-based deployment provides standardized packaging for Red Hat AI Inference with configurable values for model selection, resource allocation, and integration settings.

Authenticate to Red Hat Helm chart registry using subscription credentials. Add Helm repository and update repository indexes. Create values.yaml specifying model OCI reference or path, GPU resource requests (typically 1 GPU per pod), memory limits based on model size, API service configuration, and image pull secrets. Configure replica count for horizontal scaling. Set advanced vLLM parameters through extraArgs. Apply Helm install command with custom values. Monitor pod startup using kubectl get pods and kubectl logs. Verify health checks passing and API endpoints responding. Test inference with sample request to validate deployment.

Avoid incorrect GPU resource request syntax (must be nvidia.com/gpu: N). Do not deploy without verifying GPU node capacity available. Ensure model path is accessible from pods (registry credentials, filesystem mounts). Validate Helm values against chart schema before installation. Monitor resource usage after deployment to confirm requests/limits are appropriate.

activities.name: Deploy Distributed Inference with llm-d
activities.description: Configure and deploy multi-GPU distributed inference using LLMInferenceService resources

narratives.name: Distributed Deployment Technique

narrativeContexts.context: llm-d operator orchestrates distributed inference by creating leader-worker pods, distributing model shards across GPUs, and coordinating inference requests across the distributed system.

Install llm-d operator and LeaderWorkerSet CRD if using multi-node distribution. Create LLMInferenceService custom resource specifying model OCI container, replica count, tensor parallelism size matching GPU count per replica, resource requests for GPUs and memory, and node selectors for GPU nodes. Apply CR using kubectl apply. Monitor operator logs and pod status as operator creates leader and worker pods. Verify all workers reach Running state and health checks pass. Test distributed inference by submitting requests and validating responses. Monitor GPU utilization across workers to confirm balanced load distribution.

Avoid tensor parallelism size mismatch with actual GPU count (causes deployment failure). Do not create CR before llm-d operator is installed and healthy. Ensure sufficient GPU nodes available to satisfy replica count × parallelism size. Verify network policies allow worker-to-worker communication. Monitor model loading logs for memory errors indicating insufficient GPU memory.

activities.name: Configure Performance Monitoring
activities.description: Set up Prometheus metrics collection, Grafana dashboards, and alerting for inference services

narratives.name: Monitoring Configuration Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Comprehensive performance monitoring enables operations teams to track service health, identify performance degradation, detect anomalies, and optimize resource utilization through metrics, dashboards, and alerting.

Create ServiceMonitor resource instructing Prometheus to scrape metrics from inference service pods at /metrics endpoint. Design Grafana dashboards visualizing latency percentiles (P50, P90, P95, P99), throughput (requests/second, tokens/second), GPU utilization and memory, request error rates, and queue depths. Define Prometheus alerting rules for critical thresholds (P99 latency > 500ms, error rate > 1%, GPU memory > 95%). Configure alert routing to PagerDuty for critical alerts, Slack for warnings. Establish performance baseline by collecting metrics from representative production traffic and documenting normal operating ranges.

Avoid setting alert thresholds without baseline data (causes false alarms). Do not create dashboards without understanding which metrics indicate issues. Ensure ServiceMonitor label selectors match service labels. Verify Prometheus has sufficient retention for trend analysis (minimum 15 days). Test alerting rules fire correctly before relying on them for incident response.

activities.name: Troubleshoot Inference Issues
activities.description: Diagnose and resolve failures in distributed inference deployments using logs and diagnostics

narratives.name: Troubleshooting Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Systematic troubleshooting of distributed inference requires log correlation across components, understanding failure patterns (GPU errors, OOM, network issues), and applying diagnostic procedures to isolate root causes.

Begin diagnosis by collecting high-level status using kubectl get pods, kubectl describe for events, and recent error logs. Examine leader pod logs for orchestration issues and worker pod logs for GPU access or memory errors. Common patterns include OOM errors indicating insufficient GPU memory (reduce batch size or model size), GPU device errors (check nvidia-smi output), network timeouts between workers (validate network policies), and model loading failures (verify registry access and model format). Correlate logs across leader and workers using request IDs or timestamps. Apply systematic elimination testing each potential cause. Document resolution steps in runbook for future incidents.

Avoid assuming root cause without log evidence. Do not restart pods immediately as this destroys diagnostic data. Check GPU node health with nvidia-smi before assuming application issue. Verify network policies allow required communication. Test configuration changes in non-production before applying to production. Document incident details for post-mortem analysis.

activities.name: Integrate with Enterprise Systems
activities.description: Integrate inference services with enterprise security, monitoring, and operational tooling

narratives.name: Enterprise Integration Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise integration aligns AI inference deployment with organizational security standards, operational tooling, and governance frameworks through RBAC, network policies, monitoring federation, and compliance controls.

Configure RBAC policies granting minimal required permissions to inference service accounts. Define network policies isolating inference workloads from unauthorized access while allowing necessary communication. Integrate monitoring with enterprise Prometheus federation or commercial tools (Datadog, Dynatrace). Connect logging to enterprise SIEM (Splunk, ELK stack). If using service mesh, configure Istio/Linkerd for mTLS and traffic management. Integrate identity provider for SSO (LDAP, Active Directory, OAuth2). Configure API gateway for external access (Kong, 3scale). Validate compliance controls (audit logging, data encryption, access controls). Document integration architecture and obtain security approval.

Avoid overly permissive RBAC (violates least privilege). Do not skip network policy testing (can block legitimate traffic). Ensure monitoring integration does not introduce performance overhead. Verify compliance requirements before deployment. Test disaster recovery procedures. Document all integrations for operations team.

activities.name: Enable Tool Calling Extensions
activities.description: Configure and enable function calling support for agentic AI applications

narratives.name: Tool Calling Configuration Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Tool calling capabilities enable AI models to interact with external systems and functions, supporting agentic AI applications that combine language understanding with concrete actions through structured function invocation.

Verify model architecture supports tool calling natively (not all models have this capability). Enable tool calling features in vLLM configuration using enable-auto-tool-choice parameter. Configure chat template settings to properly format tool definitions in requests. Define tool schemas describing available functions with names, descriptions, and parameter specifications. Test tool calling by submitting requests with tool definitions and verifying model generates valid function calls. Validate that tool calling responses follow expected JSON schema. Monitor tool calling accuracy and error handling. Document tool definitions and integration patterns for application developers.

Avoid using models without native tool calling support (results in poor performance). Do not skip schema validation for tool definitions (invalid schemas cause errors). Ensure application code correctly parses tool calling responses. Test error handling for invalid tool calls. Monitor tool calling latency as it adds processing overhead. Provide clear documentation and examples to developers.

activities.description: Analyze GPU usage patterns and configure autoscaling for cost-efficient operations

narratives.name: Performance Optimization Technique

narrativeContexts.context: Inference optimization balances performance requirements against infrastructure costs through efficient resource utilization, intelligent autoscaling, and continuous performance tuning based on production usage patterns.

Analyze inference request patterns to identify traffic variation (peak vs off-peak, weekday vs weekend). Measure actual GPU utilization during different time periods to identify underutilized capacity. Implement Horizontal Pod Autoscaler based on custom metrics (requests/second, GPU utilization, queue depth). Right-size GPU instances by testing different instance types for price-performance ratio. Configure batch processing for latency-tolerant workloads to maximize GPU utilization. Establish scheduled scaling for predictable traffic patterns (scale up before daily peak, scale down overnight). Calculate cost per inference request and cost per 1M tokens. Monitor cost trends and optimization impact. Implement cluster autoscaler to add/remove GPU nodes based on pod scheduling pressure.

Avoid autoscaling on CPU metrics alone (not indicative of GPU workload). Do not set aggressive scale-down policies that cause thrashing. Ensure minimum replica count maintains availability during scale-down. Test autoscaling behavior under load before production. Monitor cost impact of autoscaling decisions. Balance cost savings against performance SLAs.

activities.name: Validate Platform for Inference Workloads
activities.description: Execute validation tests confirming platform ready to run production AI inference workloads

narrativeContexts.context: Platform validation confirms all components (GPU operators, networking, storage, monitoring) function correctly and perform adequately for production inference workloads.

Deploy test inference workload requesting GPU resources and verify successful scheduling to GPU nodes. Execute test inference requests and measure response latency. Verify GPU resources visible and allocatable via kubectl describe nodes. Test network bandwidth between GPU nodes using iperf or similar tools. Validate storage performance for model loading using fio benchmarks. Confirm platform monitoring collecting metrics from test workload. Document validation results with evidence that all criteria met.

Avoid skipping validation tests assuming platform works. Do not validate with non-representative workload (e.g., CPU-only). Ensure test workload size similar to production models. Verify network bandwidth sufficient for distributed inference. Test storage IOPS meet model loading requirements. Document baseline performance for future comparison.

activities.name: Decommission Inference Platform
activities.description: Systematically decommission inference platform with workload migration and resource reclamation

narrativeContexts.context: Platform decommissioning safely migrates workloads to alternative infrastructure while reclaiming resources and maintaining service availability during transition.

Create migration plan identifying target platform and migration schedule. Communicate decommissioning timeline to stakeholders. Migrate inference services to target platform using blue-green or canary deployment patterns. Verify migrated services operational and meeting SLAs. Drain GPU nodes and cordon to prevent new pod scheduling. Delete inference service deployments and associated resources. Uninstall GPU operators and related components. Release GPU nodes back to cluster or cloud provider. Disable monitoring for decommissioned platform. Document decommissioning completion and lessons learned.

Avoid decommissioning without migration plan (causes service outages). Do not delete resources before verifying migration successful. Ensure all data backed up before resource deletion. Communicate timeline clearly to avoid surprise. Test migration in non-production first. Document dependencies on decommissioned platform.

activities.name: Define Distributed Inference Requirements
activities.description: Analyze model characteristics and define hardware, network, and topology requirements for distributed inference

narrativeContexts.context: Requirements definition translates model characteristics into specific hardware and infrastructure needs, determining distributed architecture scope and complexity.

Calculate model memory footprint including weights and KV cache for expected context length. Determine minimum GPU count by dividing model size by per-GPU memory capacity (accounting for 80-90% utilization). Specify GPU type requirements based on model precision (FP16, INT8, INT4) and performance targets. Calculate network bandwidth requirements for inter-GPU communication (higher for pipeline parallelism). Define storage requirements for model weights (typically 2-4x model size for caching). Document latency and throughput SLA targets. Identify whether single-node multi-GPU or multi-node distribution is required.

Avoid underestimating memory requirements (forgetting KV cache overhead). Do not select GPU types without considering model precision support. Ensure network bandwidth calculations account for peak throughput. Verify GPU availability in target cluster or cloud region. Consider cost implications of GPU selection.

activities.name: Close Deployment Lifecycle
activities.description: Finalize deployment documentation, complete handoff, and archive deployment artifacts

narrativeContexts.context: Deployment lifecycle closure ensures complete documentation, successful operational handoff, and capture of lessons learned for future deployments.

Finalize all deployment documentation including architecture diagrams, configuration files, and operational procedures. Complete handoff to operations team with training and knowledge transfer. Archive deployment artifacts in version control and documentation repository. Conduct post-deployment review capturing lessons learned, issues encountered, and improvements for next deployment. Update deployment templates and automation based on lessons learned. Verify monitoring and alerting operational and transferred to operations team. Obtain formal signoff from operations team accepting responsibility for ongoing operations.

Avoid incomplete documentation handoff (causes operational issues). Do not skip lessons learned capture (wastes learning opportunity). Ensure operations team trained before handoff. Verify all runbooks and procedures tested. Document known issues and workarounds clearly. Archive all configuration and automation code.

activities.name: Configure Logging Infrastructure
activities.description: Deploy log collection and aggregation infrastructure for inference service troubleshooting

narrativeContexts.context: Logging infrastructure provides diagnostic data foundation enabling rapid troubleshooting through centralized log collection, search, and correlation across distributed components.

Deploy log collector (Fluentd, Fluent Bit, or OpenShift logging operator) as DaemonSet on all nodes. Configure log collection from all inference service pods including leader and workers. Set appropriate log levels (INFO for normal operations, DEBUG for troubleshooting). Configure log aggregation to central storage (Loki, Elasticsearch, or cloud logging service). Define log retention policy based on storage capacity and compliance requirements (typically 30-90 days). Enable log search and filtering capabilities through Grafana Loki or Kibana. Implement log correlation using request IDs or trace IDs for distributed request tracking. Test log collection by generating test logs and verifying they appear in aggregation system.

Avoid excessive DEBUG logging in production (performance impact and storage costs). Do not collect logs without retention policy (storage exhaustion). Ensure log collector has sufficient resources (CPU, memory). Verify log timestamps synchronized across nodes. Test log search performance with representative query patterns. Document log schema and important log patterns for troubleshooting.

activities.name: Plan Enterprise Integration
activities.description: Define integration approach for target enterprise platform with security and compliance requirements

narrativeContexts.context: Integration planning aligns AI inference deployment with enterprise platform standards, security requirements, and operational tooling through comprehensive architecture design and stakeholder alignment.

Identify target platform (OpenShift, AKS, GKE, CoreWeave) and document platform-specific requirements. Gather integration requirements from enterprise architecture (SSO, API gateway, service mesh, monitoring). Document security and compliance requirements (RBAC policies, network isolation, encryption, audit logging). Design network architecture including ingress/egress patterns, service mesh integration, and DNS configuration. Define access control model aligning with enterprise identity management. Create integration architecture diagram showing all touchpoints. Review architecture with security, compliance, and platform teams. Obtain architecture approval before proceeding to implementation.

Avoid skipping stakeholder alignment (causes rework during implementation). Do not assume standard patterns work without validation (platform-specific constraints exist). Ensure security requirements gathered from security team, not assumed. Verify compliance requirements early (late discovery causes delays). Document all integration points clearly. Test architecture assumptions with proof-of-concept if novel patterns used.

activities.name: Verify Compliance Controls
activities.description: Validate deployment meets regulatory and organizational compliance requirements with evidence collection

narrativeContexts.context: Compliance verification ensures inference deployment meets regulatory requirements (SOC2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR) through systematic validation and evidence collection.

Review applicable compliance frameworks and identify required controls for AI inference (data encryption, access logging, data residency, retention policies). Validate technical controls implemented (encryption at rest and in transit, RBAC policies, network segmentation, audit logging). Collect evidence for each control (configuration screenshots, policy documents, audit logs). Verify data governance policies applied (data classification, handling procedures, retention schedules). Test incident response procedures to validate detection and response capabilities. Generate compliance documentation including control matrix mapping requirements to implementations. Obtain compliance attestation from compliance team or external auditor. Address any identified gaps before production deployment.

Avoid assuming compliance without validation (audit findings cause production delays). Do not collect evidence without understanding compliance requirements. Ensure audit logging captures all required events. Verify data residency requirements met (geographic restrictions). Test compliance controls work as expected (theoretical vs actual). Document evidence clearly for auditors.

activities.name: Establish Production Support
activities.description: Integrate support ticketing, change management, and operational procedures for production operations

narrativeContexts.context: Production support establishment integrates inference operations with enterprise support processes, change management workflows, and operational tooling ensuring operational excellence.

Integrate support ticket system (ServiceNow, Jira Service Desk) with inference service monitoring for automated ticket creation on critical alerts. Configure change management workflows requiring CAB approval for production changes. Establish backup and recovery procedures including backup frequency, restore testing, and recovery time objectives. Document and test disaster recovery plan including failover procedures and RPO/RTO targets. Configure SLA monitoring and reporting dashboards for business stakeholders. Create operational runbooks covering routine maintenance, scaling procedures, and upgrade processes. Establish on-call rotation with escalation procedures to vendor support. Conduct operational readiness review with all stakeholders before production launch.

Avoid launching production without tested backup/recovery procedures (data loss risk). Do not integrate ticketing without testing (alert noise or missed incidents). Ensure change management process does not block urgent fixes (emergency change procedures needed). Verify disaster recovery procedures tested, not just documented. Train operations team on all support procedures before production. Document escalation paths clearly including vendor support contacts.
